title: Quality Metrics for LLM-Generated Asset Administration Shells: A Perturbation-Based Evaluation Approach
abstract: arXiv:2609.07290v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The rapid digital transformation of manufacturing, often referred to as Industry 4.0, relies on seamless interoperability between physical and software assets. A central enabler is the Asset Administration Shell (AAS), a standardized digital representation of such assets. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) enable the generation of AAS submodels from unstructured sources such as product datasheets but raise challenges for quality assurance. In particular, unexpected errors, the lack of ground truth references, and the absence of standardized quality metrics hinder reliable adoption. In this work, we evaluate quality metrics for AI-generated AAS using a perturbation-based evaluation framework. By systematically degrading AAS generation along multiple dimensions, we assess how well different metrics reflect quality changes. Based on a dataset of 200 products from multiple manufacturers, we generate 6,400 AAS instances using G

tldr: 本文提出一种基于扰动的评估框架，通过在多个维度上系统性地降低大语言模型生成的资产管理壳（AAS）质量，来评估不同质量度量指标反映质量变化的有效性，从而为AI生成的AAS建立可靠的质量保证方法。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a perturbation-based evaluation framework that systematically degrades LLM-generated Asset Administration Shells (AAS) along multiple dimensions to assess how well different quality metrics reflect quality changes, establishing a reliable quality assurance approach for AI-generated AAS.
